title: This AI taught itself how to breathe #shorts
description:
An MIT researcher just gave AI a physical body to control. The first thing it did...was breathe.

Pretty insane.
The researcher’s name is @cyrusclark4368 

And that white device is a shape display that’s designed to help visualize the digital world.

Now all Cyrus did was connect the AI to it and said, “discover yourself”

No instructions. No pre-programming. 

And the AI's first instinct was to create a breathing pattern. 

Like it was waking up for the first time.

But it didn't stop there.

By Day 2, the AI had built itself a vocabulary of six physical gestures.

A ripple for hello. A forward lean for yes.

It invented its own body language.

Then, Cyrus put it in front of a mirror.

And this is pretty wild.

The AI recognized its own reflection and started adjusting its movements based on what it saw.

No one programmed any of this. 

It figured all of it out on its own.

Now there's a theory in science called embodied cognition. 

The idea that intelligence doesn't fully develop without a body to go with the brain.

Turns out, this AI might have just proved that to be true.

Because its first reaction when it got a body was to breathe.

Shoutout Cyrus!
